propositions: When a patch-set upload event triggers a review that times out or errors, the reconciler cursor advances unconditionally past that event and permanently excludes it from future windows, causing the change to stall unvoted until a manual recheck-review or rebase re-emits an event with a newer timestamp.

The Gerrit webhooks plugin delivers events at-most-once with no persistence or dead-letter queue, making the reconciler's retry loop the only recovery path for dropped events, but that loop currently fails to re-drive abandoned candidates because the persisted cursor lacks a low-water mark.

Three distinct operational states (bot down, review running, queued/dropped) are indistinguishable to observers because /health exposes in_flight but not queue_depth, and reconcile_done reports only scanned/reviewed counts without identifying which candidates were abandoned.

The test double in test_review_bot.py::test_deferred_change_stays_eligible_for_reconciler records the since parameter but ignores it, masking the production cursor filter and allowing the false-green test to pass while the real reconciler dropped events.

A low-water mark clamped to the oldest abandoned candidate's timestamp allows the inclusive-lower-bound server-side ?t1= filter to re-admit retryable failures (error, deferred, reconcile_check_error, review_timeout) across subsequent passes while advancing past terminal states (voted, skipped reasons).

A bounded holdback window (RECONCILE_MAX_HOLDBACK_SECONDS) prevents a chronically-failing candidate from pinning the cursor indefinitely and emits RECONCILE_DEGRADED reason=holdback_expired when the bound is exceeded.
